title: Choke names, constrictions and markings
summary: From cylinder to full: typical constrictions in millimetres and thou, the 1/4–1/2–3/4 fractions and the star marks used in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting. Values are approximate and differ between makers.

body.html: Names come from English, from open to tight: cylinder, skeet, improved cylinder, light modified, modified, improved modified, full. Europeans often say them as fractions: quarter (improved cylinder), half (modified), three-quarter (improved modified) and full. Many Italian guns mark chokes with stars, and there the rule is upside down: more stars means a more open choke.
Below are typical constrictions for 12 gauge. One thou is a thousandth of an inch, about 0.025 mm. Real values depend on the maker and even on the bore of the particular barrel.

html: Skeet: a very light constriction, about 0.1–0.15 mm (4–6 thou); in Europe sometimes called 1/8.
Improved cylinder (IC): about 0.25 mm (around 10 thou), in Europe 1/4, a quarter choke.
Light modified (LM): about 0.35–0.4 mm (around 15 thou), sometimes marked 3/8.
Modified (M): about 0.5 mm (around 20 thou), 1/2, a half choke.
Full: about 0.9–1 mm (35–40 thou), 1/1 or simply Full. Tighter chokes (extra full) exist, but clay shooting rarely needs them.

body.html: The fractions are handy in conversation, but they are not exact millimetres: one maker's 1/2 may differ slightly from another's.

Italian makers, Beretta for example, use star marks: five stars for cylinder, four for improved cylinder (1/4), three for modified (1/2), two for improved modified (3/4) and one for full. Skeet chokes carry no stars. Other makers cut notches on the rim of the tube, use coloured bands or print the name (IC, M, LM).
The most reliable source is the marking on the choke itself or the gun's manual. If in doubt, a gunsmith can measure the constriction with a gauge in a minute.

key_points.html: Cylinder 0 · Skeet ~0.1–0.15 mm · IC ~0.25 mm (1/4) · LM ~0.35–0.4 mm
Fractions: quarter = improved cylinder, half = modified, three-quarter = improved modified, full.
Stars: the more stars, the more open the choke.
Values are approximate and differ between makers.

did_you_know.html: Modern competition barrels are often 'overbored': the inside is made slightly wider than the standard for the gauge. So the same choke with the same name can give a slightly different constriction in different guns: what counts is the difference between bore and choke.

quiz.q: What is the approximate constriction of a modified (1/2) choke in 12 gauge?
quiz.explain: Modified is about 0.5 mm, or around 20 thou.

quiz.q: What does a choke marked with four stars mean on a Beretta gun?
quiz.explain: In the star system, the more stars the more open the choke: four stars is improved cylinder.

quiz.q: In European usage, which choke is a 'half'?
quiz.explain: Half (1/2) is modified; quarter is improved cylinder, three-quarter is improved modified.
